results.verified_title: Europe’s research dilemma – balancing security and scientific cooperation with China
results.source_identity_basis: Opened MERICS commentary by Altynay Junusova and Antonia Hmaidi, published 18 March 2026; title, organisation, date, and link match the manifest.
results.evidence_location: Introduction and discussion of research security, Horizon 2026–27 and research-cooperation tradeoffs
results.specific_finding: European research actors are balancing continued scientific exchange with China against dual-use and knowledge-transfer security controls, with new Horizon Europe 2026–27 China participation limits.
results.primary_evidence_summary: MERICS sections on dual-use research, EU security instruments, China cooperation and national implementation differences. The work cites sensitive Earth-observation and other cooperation but does not independently quantify knowledge leakage.
results.corroboration_assessment: Independent Council recommendation establishes the EU research-security policy; EURAXESS describes 2026–27 programme eligibility restrictions. Neither verifies every illustrative MERICS dual-use case.
results.mechanism_and_ri_importance: Structural governance change: heightened risk assessment and conditional eligibility may alter cross-border science partnerships and collaboration overhead.
results.eu_radar_comparison: Existing main-Radar record (A: Europe’s research dilemma – balancing security and scientific cooperation with China). Independently checked; confirms the limited factual structural finding stated here, not every claim on the original page.
results.method_and_limitations: Commentary and policy analysis, not original empirical measurement. China-specific threat anecdotes and each member state’s implementation require project-level verification.

results.verified_title: Ukraine bets on research talent and a thriving startup sector
results.source_identity_basis: Opened European Commission Directorate-General R&I feature dated 5 May 2026 and independently opened the Ukrainian national researchers portal follow-up of 30 October 2026.
results.source_type: European Commission feature plus implementation update
results.evidence_location: European Commission article: research talent and national support sections; nauka.gov.ua 30 October 2026 first four paragraphs
results.specific_finding: Ukraine implemented a competitive researcher-retention scholarship scheme: 2,650 state scholarships allocated; 1,934 first-wave recipients approved for October 2026–September 2028 at UAH 10,000 per month. This updates the earlier European Commission estimate of 2,625 planned awards.
results.primary_evidence_summary: European Commission 5 May feature discusses retaining talent, support for researchers and startups. National portal 30 October, paragraphs 1–4, explicitly records approved list, total capacity, term and monthly stipend.
results.corroboration_assessment: The Ukrainian ministry-affiliated national portal corroborates the launch with administrative details and supersedes the earlier planned total; it is official implementation evidence rather than an impact evaluation.
results.mechanism_and_ri_importance: Researcher retention and predictable supplementary payments counter wartime erosion of national R&I human capital; this is actual awards issued, not merely a programme announcement.
results.eu_radar_comparison: Existing Radar note is now outdated in one numeric detail: later official awards show 2,650 places, not initial 2,625 estimate, plus first-wave approval of 1,934; this changes and extends source context.
results.method_and_limitations: Number of awarded scholarships is an administrative output, not proof of retention, startup formation or researcher productivity. 2,650 are allocated positions, not all awarded.
results.reviewer_notes: Date-sensitive correction: programme launched with 2,625 cited earlier vs 2,650 total positions now recorded; 1,934 is recipients first wave, not total.

results.evidence_location: FAPESP researcher quotation on prototype status; Yan et al. PDF p.1 abstract, framework and data section
results.specific_finding: Brazilian research team demonstrated non-invasive UAV image analysis of Nellore feedlot cattle morphology and growth over 112 days using machine vision; FAPESP’s commercial slaughter-timing framing remains an envisaged application rather than validated deployment.
results.primary_evidence_summary: FAPESP story says a working prototype was still under development; archived peer-reviewed paper page 1 abstract and methods report YOLOv11s, SAM 2.1, cattle morphology extraction and 112-day growth modelling.

results.eu_radar_comparison: Not identified in main Radar per package manifest. This is a coverage comparison only, not proof of an overlooked trend.
results.method_and_limitations: Single feedlot/species observational case; morphology as proxy for economics, no independent economic or welfare outcome trial, likely domain shift across herds/cameras/conditions. FAPESP future-product pitch is not a deployed service.

results.verified_title: Frontlines and faultlines: how the Russo-Ukrainian conflict reshapes the landscape of scientific research
results.source_identity_basis: Journal citation to Yang Ding, 6 July 2026 Humanities and Social Sciences Communications title identified; opened complete author-uploaded original preprint PDF arXiv 2606.01124, same title/author and research summary, and separately reviewed independent 2026 Web of Science-based bibliometric research.
results.source_type: quantitative peer-reviewed article, read through identical-author preprint; independent bibliometrics
results.evidence_location: arXiv full PDF pp.1,7–8,36–37 and supplemental audit; PMC full article Abstract, Methods and International Collaboration Patterns
results.specific_finding: Across 2000–2023 publication/affiliation metadata, the author identifies dislocation of Russian and Ukrainian scholars, shifts in topics and a move in collaboration patterns away from Russia–Ukraine / Russia–West relationships following 2014 and 2022. Independent datasets support significant Ukraine-related publication/collaboration disruptions but differ in definitions and magnitudes.
results.primary_evidence_summary: Yang Ding arXiv PDF p.1 abstract, pp.7–8 methods, p.37 limitations; dataset: 272,924 Ukraine-linked records and 1,533,758 Russia-linked records. Kreslova et al. 2026 paper analyzes independent Web of Science / InCites series 1991–2024, documenting post-2022 Ukraine decline and collaboration shifts.
results.corroboration_assessment: Independent bibliometric papers corroborate broad collaboration disruption while adding nuance: Russian coauthorship share can be steadier than raw publication counts, so avoid simplistic sanctions-causality attribution.
results.mechanism_and_ri_importance: Conflict shocks to R&I systems alter talent locations, specialties, and network structure, and affect capacity beyond physical infrastructure losses.
results.eu_radar_comparison: Not identified in main Radar per package manifest. This is a coverage comparison only, not proof of an overlooked trend.
results.method_and_limitations: OpenAlex metadata (migration inferred from affiliations; author disambiguation), 2023 cutoff and publication lags; authors themselves caution the results are not definitive causal effects. Other Web of Science-based comparisons use different journal coverage. Original journal page blocked; exact author preprint used.
results.reviewer_notes: Journal site access restricted. Exact title and Yang Ding authorship match paper; preprint used for all methodological/results details; no causal sanctions claim.
